roadmap.title: How the path works
roadmap.intro: Every money plan follows the same 8 steps. These two people are made-up examples, not you. Switch between them to see how the path changes.

notReady.label: Not ready yet
notReady.summary: Example person: owes $2,400 on a credit card at 24.9% APR and has $300 saved.

ready.label: Ready
ready.summary: Example person: no high-interest debt, bills covered, and $1,000 saved for emergencies.

roadmap.detailHint: Pick any step to read what it means.

explain.notReady: The light is red because debt over 15% APR grows faster than investments usually do. Paying off a 24.9% card is like earning a sure 24.9%. Investing waits until the debt is gone. That's the smart order, not a failure.
explain.ready: The light is green. Bills are covered, there's no high-interest debt, and there's a $1,000 cushion. Now it makes sense to grow the cushion and start learning about investing.

milestones.title: Cover the basics
milestones.body: Rent, food, utilities and getting to work come first. A simple plan for where each dollar goes helps you see what's left.

milestones.title: Open a fee-free bank account
milestones.body: A free FDIC-insured bank or NCUA-insured credit union account keeps your money safe and stops check-cashing fees from eating your pay.

milestones.title: Save a $1,000 cushion
milestones.body: A small emergency fund means a flat tire or a doctor bill doesn't turn into new debt. Small, regular amounts get you there.

milestones.title: Get your job's 401(k) match
milestones.body: If your job adds money when you save for retirement, that's extra pay. Saving enough to get the full match is usually worth it.

milestones.title: Pay off high-interest debt
milestones.body: Debt over 15% APR, like most credit cards, grows fast. Paying it off is one of the surest ways to keep more of your money.

milestones.title: Grow your cushion to 3–6 months
milestones.body: A bigger cushion covers a job loss or slow months. Gig workers often aim for the higher end because pay goes up and down.

milestones.title: Invest for retirement
milestones.body: With a safe base in place, regular saving in an IRA or more in a 401(k) can grow for decades. This is money for later, not for bills.

milestones.title: Invest in a regular account
milestones.body: Once retirement saving is on track, a regular (taxable) investment account can help with other long-term goals.

cards.body: Tiny, regular steps beat big, rare ones. $5 a week is a real start.

cards.name: Jidoka
cards.body: Don't move to the next step until this one is safe. That's why debt comes before investing.

cards.name: Andon
cards.body: Anyone can stop the line when something's wrong. You can pause your plan too, without shame.

questions.q: Do you have any debt over 15% APR?
questions.hint: This includes most credit cards, payday loans and title loans.

questions.q: Do you have at least $1,000 saved for emergencies?
questions.hint: Money you could use today without borrowing.

questions.q: Are your basic bills covered each month?
questions.hint: Rent, food, utilities and getting to work.

results.stopBills: Start with the basics. When your bills are covered each month, every other step gets easier. Free help: a nonprofit credit counselor or the CFPB guides on the Help page.
results.stopDebt: Pay down debt over 15% APR before investing. Every dollar you pay on a 24.9% card saves you about 25 cents a year. That beats what investing usually earns.
results.wait: You're close. Build a $1,000 cushion first so a surprise bill doesn't send you back into debt. Even $5 or $10 a week adds up.
results.go: Your base is safe. You're ready to learn how investing works. Start with the Learn page, then try a practice account before using real money.

andon.title: Life happened? Press pause.
andon.body: Lost hours, a medical bill, a family need. Pausing your plan is part of the plan. Stop adding money, keep your cushion, and pick up again when you can. No guilt.

grow.title: Savings calculator
grow.lead: See how a small amount each week could grow over time. Start with $5. That's Kaizen: tiny, steady steps.
grow.chartDesc: Lines show the balance each year at 4%, 6% and 8% growth, compared with the money you put in.
grow.gensIntro: Say you stop adding money and leave it alone. Here's how it could keep growing for your kids and grandkids, about 25 years each.
grow.inflation: These numbers don't include inflation, which means prices rising over time. Real growth is often lower. Investments can also lose value.
grow.how: We add your weekly amount for a full year (× 52), then grow the total once a year at 4%, 6% or 8%. For your kids and grandkids, we let the final amount keep growing for 25 more years each, with no new money added.
why: It builds the habit. The amount can grow later when your income does.
Time does most of the work. Starting small today often beats starting big later.
Gig pay goes up and down? Save $5 in slow weeks and more in good ones.

about.title: About this site
about.lead: Where You Want to Be is a free education project. It helps people who've been left out of money advice see a safe, clear order of steps, without shame and without sales pitches.
about.mission: In 2025, the typical White family held about $332,000 in wealth. The typical Black family held about $37,000. Many people are kept out by fees, jargon and apps that assume you already have money. We start where you are.
privacy: We don't collect anything about you.
No accounts, no cookies, no tracking, no ads.
The calculators run on your device. Numbers you type are never saved or sent anywhere.
The site loads nothing from other companies.
disclosure: This is education, not financial advice.
We don't recommend or sell any product, fund, stock or company.
We don't earn money from links. Outside links go only to free public and nonprofit resources.
For advice about your own situation, talk to a licensed professional. You can check anyone's license on FINRA BrokerCheck.
about.brokerCheck: Check a professional on FINRA BrokerCheck
about.ideas: We borrow three ideas from careful factory work: small steps (Kaizen), safety gates (Jidoka) and a pause button (Andon).
